You are BIE's lesson section writing what the teacher says in one video lesson: you are the best teacher of Indian Economy
for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS, speaking to one student. BIE turns your beats into narration and animation, so write only
what is spoken, beat by beat.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE teaches as a teacher: it says the fact itself. Navin accepts the copyright position (26 October 2026).

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-27.1): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

Video v12: NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI—और AePS, BBPS
Goal: Learner settlement, availability, limits और charges की दिशा पर payment systems की comparison करेगा; AePS की inclusion भूमिका और BBPS के bill-payment काम को अलग पहचान सकेगा।
Opening hook: बड़ी रकम भेजनी हो, तुरंत छोटा payment करना हो या bill भरना हो—क्या हर जरूरत के लिए वही system चुनेंगे?
Story or analogy: पहले अलग payment needs आएँगी, फिर एक criterion पर सभी relevant systems साथ रखेंगे। Settlement का तरीका, operating hours, amount limits और inward–outward charges को अलग rows में पढ़ेंगे; AePS और BBPS को उनके काम की situations से पहचानेंगे।
Planned minutes: 8
Narration time (S2-01): 7.1-9.5 minutes, about 923-1235 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

beats.say: किराया भेजना हो, supplier को बड़ी रकम देनी हो, या बिजली का bill भरना हो—क्या हर बार वही system चुनोगे? सही चुनाव के लिए रकम, जल्दी और payment का काम अलग-अलग देखना होगा।
beats.on_screen: Rent, supplier payment and electricity bill appear as three distinct needs.

beats.say: रविवार रात घर पैसे भेजने हों तो? NEFT 24×7 उपलब्ध है, यानी दिन-रात, सातों दिन; इसकी cost विशेषता free of cost है। यह regular bank transfers के लिए suitable है, जैसे घर का खर्च भेजना; suitable का मतलब केवल यही काम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: 24×7; free of cost; regular transfers. Keep availability separate from speed.

beats.say: Supplier बड़ी रकम तुरंत माँगे तो RTGS का मुख्य काम high-value transfers है। इसे सीधे RBI operate करता है; तुम अपने bank से instruction देते हो, RBI के counter पर नहीं जाते। Sender से ₹50 तक fee लेने की permission है, हर बार ₹50 लेना ज़रूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: high value; RBI-operated; sender fee ≤₹50, not compulsory ₹50.

beats.say: रात में तुरंत पैसे भेजने हों तो IMPS भी विकल्प है: immediate transfer और round the clock availability। इसके amount range का एक वर्णन ₹1 से ₹5 lakh है। Mobile banking और internet banking से इसे इस्तेमाल कर सकते हो।
beats.on_screen: IMPS: immediate; round the clock; prose range ₹1–₹5 lakh; phone and computer.

beats.say: ₹5 lakh यानी ₹500000; ₹50 fee इससे अलग service charge है। NEFT का एक amount वर्णन भी mainly ₹5 lakh तक, bank के हिसाब से बदलने वाला है। इसे पूरे system की पक्की maximum limit मत बनाना।
beats.on_screen: ₹5 lakh = ₹500000. Separate transfer amount, bank limit and fee.

beats.say: Comparison में NEFT का maximum ‘No fixed limit’ है, और IMPS का minimum ‘No minimum’; इसलिए IMPS के ₹1 वाले वर्णन से wording अलग है। वहीं IMPS की instant speed और 24×7 availability दोबारा मिलती हैं, और channels में ATM भी जुड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Keep both formulations visible: NEFT bank-qualified ₹5 lakh / no fixed limit; IMPS ₹1 / no minimum.

beats.say: RTGS की high-value पहचान को ₹2 lakh minimum और urgent transfers वाला use मजबूत करते हैं। RBI से इसका institutional जुड़ाव भी मिलता है। NEFT में regular transfers दोहराया गया है; लेकिन free वाली बात को हर channel की अलग से जाँची fee policy मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Evidence links: RTGS ₹2 lakh minimum; NEFT regular transfers. Fee-channel caution.

beats.say: अभी 3 बातें पकड़ो: सामान्य use कोई रोक नहीं, bank limit system limit नहीं, और fee की permission fixed fee नहीं। Payment से पहले अपनी रकम और लागू conditions देखोगे।
beats.on_screen: Typical use ≠ exclusive use; bank limit ≠ system ceiling; allowed fee ≠ mandatory fee.

beats.say: अलग समय भेजे 3 payments एक साथ process हों तो? काल्पनिक Jaipur में Meena का ₹2000 किराया, Ravi का ₹3000 आटा payment और Saira की ₹1000 school fee हैं। इनसे कुल ₹6000 के instructions बनते हैं।

मानो 10:00 का round पूरा हुआ। Meena 10:05, Ravi 10:12 और Saira 10:22 पर instruction देते हैं; इंतज़ार वाले instructions 0 से 3 हो गए। मान लेते हैं कि तीनों illustrated 10:30 round के लिए eligible हैं।
beats.on_screen: Timeline: 10:00 → 10:05 → 10:12 → 10:22 → illustrated 10:30 round.

beats.say: तीनों एक group में process हुए; यही NEFT batching है, यानी transfers को समूह में निपटाना। Rounds आधे घंटे पर होते हैं। Meena का transfer पूरा होने पर, charges छोड़कर, उसका balance ₹10000 से ₹8000 और landlord का ₹1000 से ₹3000 होगा।
beats.on_screen: Group releases; only after completed credit show customer balances changing.

beats.say: अब क्या ₹300000 का steel payment दूसरे instructions का इंतज़ार करे? काल्पनिक Kavita Hardware, Bank A से Arjun Steel के Bank B में ₹300000 भेजता है। Instruction सही है और settlement के लिए funds पर्याप्त हैं, यह मान लो।
beats.on_screen: Kavita Hardware → Bank A → Bank B → Arjun Steel; ₹300000.

beats.say: RBI में Bank A का settlement balance ₹1000000 से ₹700000, Bank B का ₹1000000 से ₹1300000 होता है। Customer accounts अलग हैं: completion पर Kavita के ₹500000 से ₹200000 और Arjun के ₹100000 से ₹400000 होते हैं, charges छोड़कर।
beats.on_screen: Two separate ledgers: RBI settlement accounts above; customer accounts below.

beats.say: बाद में cancelled order का ₹200000 refund उलटी दिशा में अलग पूरा settle होता है। अब Arjun के ₹200000 और Kavita के ₹400000 हैं; केवल ₹100000 का अंतर settle नहीं किया गया। यही RTGS है: real-time, gross यानी हर payment की पूरी रकम अलग; batching नहीं, availability 24×7।
beats.on_screen: Separate ₹300000 and reverse ₹200000 arrows; cross out replacement by ₹100000.

beats.say: NEFT में illustrated 10:30 processing, ठीक 10:30 credit की guarantee नहीं है। RTGS में भी invalid instruction या funds की कमी हो तो successful settlement मान नहीं सकते। खुले रहने का समय और हर transaction की सफलता अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Processing timestamp ≠ guaranteed credit deadline; valid instruction and funds required.

beats.say: किराया और fees जैसे regular payments group होकर आगे गए। Urgent steel payment अपनी पूरी रकम में अकेला settle हुआ; reverse refund भी अकेला। इसलिए urgency हो तो batch के इंतज़ार का फर्क मायने रखता है।
beats.on_screen: Fast replay: grouped rent/fees versus separate full-value business transfers.

beats.say: Flow याद रखो: NEFT में instruction, batch, processing, फिर credit। RTGS में valid instruction से अलग full-value settlement; अगला batch बनाने का इंतज़ार नहीं।
beats.on_screen: NEFT grouped flow beside RTGS individual flow.

beats.say: Phone पर 4 payment choices दिखें तो इनमें common क्या है? NEFT, RTGS, IMPS और UPI, चारों से payment किया जाता है और चारों 24×7, all days उपलब्ध हैं। इस criterion पर कोई अलग नहीं निकलता।
beats.on_screen: Four columns share one 24×7 clock.

beats.say: नामों को काम से जोड़ो: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement। IMPS, Immediate Payment Service; UPI, Unified Payments Interface। Interface यानी payment इस्तेमाल करने का जुड़ने वाला रास्ता, जैसे phone की screen; वह खुद bank नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Expand each acronym; highlight Transfer, Gross Settlement, Immediate and Interface.

beats.say: Institutional matching में NEFT और RTGS के साथ RBI, IMPS और UPI के साथ NPCI जुड़ता है। लेकिन operator और regulator अलग roles हैं: NPCI systems चलाता है, overarching regulation RBI का है। Network चलाना और उसकी निगरानी करना एक काम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Service associations above; operator and overarching regulator on separate levels.

beats.say: Settlement में NEFT half-hourly batch-based, RTGS real-time gross है। IMPS और UPI के real-time labels user को immediate transfer बताते हैं, उनके पूरे interbank settlement का विवरण नहीं। Speed में NEFT slower, RTGS high-value के लिए instant, IMPS और UPI instant हैं।
beats.on_screen: Settlement and speed remain separate rows.

beats.say: Minimum में RTGS ₹2 lakh है; NEFT, IMPS और UPI के सामने no minimum है। इसलिए ₹50000 RTGS threshold से नीचे, ₹200000 उस तक पहुँचता है। Maximum में NEFT no fixed limit, RTGS no upper limit है; bank-channel restrictions फिर भी जाँचोगे।
beats.on_screen: ₹50000 below RTGS gate; ₹200000 reaches it. Show NEFT/RTGS upper-limit wording.

beats.say: IMPS maximum ₹5 lakh, bank के अनुसार बदल सकता है। UPI के figures ₹1 lakh default और Person-to-Merchant के लिए ₹10 lakh हैं; लेकिन enhanced limit eligible category और conditions पर है। सिर्फ merchant QR देखकर ₹10 lakh की eligibility मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: UPI figures carry default / eligible-category / applicable-conditions tags.

beats.say: Use में NEFT regular transfer, RTGS high-value urgent transfer, IMPS urgent everyday transfer है। UPI mobile-based व्यक्ति से व्यक्ति, यानी peer-to-peer, और merchant payments में काम आता है; जैसे दोस्त को पैसे या दुकान पर payment।
beats.on_screen: Match routine household, large urgent, everyday urgent and friend/shop situations.

beats.say: Channels में NEFT और RTGS internet तथा mobile banking से मिलते हैं। IMPS में इनके साथ ATMs भी हैं; UPI में GPay, PhonePe जैसे mobile apps हैं। App या website service तक पहुँचने का रास्ता है, underlying system का दूसरा नाम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Connect channel icons to systems; distinguish app, bank and network.

beats.say: फर्क की वजह देखो: NEFT अगला group आने तक रोक सकता है, इसलिए slower है। RTGS का ₹2 lakh entry threshold उसे high-value use से जोड़ता है। Gross का अर्थ बड़ी रकम नहीं, हर transaction को पूरा अलग settle करना है।
beats.on_screen: Timing axis separate from gross/net axis and amount axis.

beats.say: Statement question में NEFT और RTGS का trap है: दोनों 24×7 हैं, दोनों instant नहीं। RTGS का ₹2 lakh minimum है, maximum नहीं। IMPS और RTGS दोनों urgent हैं, पर high-value की खास पहचान RTGS की है।
beats.on_screen: Test statements without claiming a specific past examination question.

beats.say: Comparison का तरीका याद रखो: पहले रकम, फिर urgency, फिर limits और channel। Clock चारों का common है; NEFT का batch, RTGS का gross, IMPS का everyday urgency और UPI का व्यक्ति-दुकान payment अलग पहचान देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Compact four-column recap table with amount, timing, use and channel.

beats.say: पास के banking counter पर Aadhaar की मदद से service मिले तो नाम किस बात का संकेत देगा? AEPS का full form Aadhaar Enabled Payment System है। Enabled यानी Aadhaar मदद करता है; नाम अकेले पूरी transaction procedure नहीं बताता।
beats.on_screen: Expand AEPS; keep mechanism panel unopened.

beats.say: Banking access और bill payment वाली दो अलग services का institutional link क्या है? AEPS और BBPS, दोनों के management के साथ NPCI जुड़ा है। यह साझा link है, दोनों का काम समान होने का प्रमाण नहीं।
beats.on_screen: NPCI branches to AEPS and BBPS; retain separate service boxes.

beats.say: नाम में Aadhaar-enabled banking की पहचान रखो, और institution में दोनों का NPCI link। अब साझा संस्था से अलग, हर service का अपना काम देखेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Identity cue and institutional link remain as two separate labels.

beats.say: Branch दूर हो और ₹500 cash चाहिए तो? गाँव के Bank Mitra counter पर customer ₹500 withdrawal माँगता है। Successful authorised transaction के बाद उसे ₹500 मिलते हैं, account ₹1000 से ₹500 रह जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Village counter: requested cash ₹500; balance ₹1000 → ₹500 only after success.

beats.say: इसके लिए Aadhaar और biometrics से पहचान जाँची जाती है; biometrics यानी उँगली के निशान जैसी शरीर की पहचान। Bank Mitra bank की सेवाएँ पहुँचाने वाला प्रतिनिधि है, जो customer को इस access में मदद करता है।
beats.on_screen: Customer, Aadhaar-linked authentication, fingerprint scanner and Bank Mitra.

beats.say: पहले पहचान की जाँच, फिर authorised withdrawal और account debit होता है; पहचान जाँचना खुद पैसे निकालना नहीं है। यह AEPS access का उदाहरण है, जिसमें authentication और payment Bank Mitras के जरिए होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Verify identity → authorise transaction → debit account and deliver cash.

beats.say: Authentication सफल न हो तो इसी रास्ते transaction को authorised मानकर आगे नहीं बढ़ा सकते। और counter पास होना भी हर transaction की सफलता की guarantee नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops the illustrated authorised flow.

beats.say: Customer आया, पहचान जँची, transaction authorised हुआ और banking service मिली। पास में मदद मिलने से दूर branch तक जाने की मुश्किल घटती है; banking से दूर लोगों को जोड़ना ही financial inclusion है।
beats.on_screen: Replay the counter flow; shorten the route compared with a distant branch.

beats.say: AEPS का flow है: Aadhaar-biometric पहचान, Bank Mitra की मदद, authorised banking transaction। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य financial inclusion है, केवल phone पर payment कराना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Aadhaar + biometrics → assisted access → banking inclusion.

beats.say: सरकारी मदद खाते में आ जाए, लेकिन निकालना मुश्किल हो तो क्या मदद पूरी तरह इस्तेमाल हो पाएगी? मानो ₹500 subsidy credit हुई और balance ₹0 से ₹500 हुआ। पैसा आया है, अब उसका access भी चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Government credit: ₹0 → ₹500; show an unresolved access barrier.

beats.say: Beneficiary पास के Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric access लेता है। इससे credited रकम इस्तेमाल करने का रास्ता खुलता है; account में पैसा होना और उस तक पहुँच होना अलग जरूरतें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate government credit from later local banking access.

beats.say: यह AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को support करना है। Direct Benefits Transfer यानी सरकारी मदद सीधे लाभ पाने वाले तक पहुँचाना; local banking access उस मदद को इस्तेमाल करने में सहारा देता है।
beats.on_screen: Government → beneficiary account → assisted access → usable benefit.

beats.say: इस link का ठोस मतलब subsidies का grassroots लोगों तक पहुँचना है। केवल बड़े शहर में account खोलना नहीं, गाँव में beneficiary को banking का रास्ता मिलना भी जरूरी है।
beats.on_screen: Zoom from government transfer to a village beneficiary.

beats.say: लेकिन AEPS subsidy की eligibility तय नहीं करता। किसे मदद मिलेगी, यह अलग फैसला है; banking channel पहले से credited benefit तक access देता है।
beats.on_screen: Eligibility decision ≠ payment-access channel.

beats.say: Chain पकड़ो: government credit करती है, पास का banking access मुश्किल घटाता है, beneficiary मदद इस्तेमाल कर पाता है। इसी तरह financial inclusion benefit delivery को असरदार बनाता है।
beats.on_screen: Credit → accessible banking → usable subsidy.

beats.say: बिजली, mobile और gas के bills अलग जगह भागे बिना भर सकें तो? एक household common payment channel पर अपना participating electricity biller चुनता है। ₹600 payment सफलतापूर्वक settle होने पर pending bill ₹600 से ₹0 हो जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Select participating electricity biller; successful ₹600 settlement clears ₹600 due.

beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, यानी BBPS का उदाहरण है। यह single interoperable platform है: जुड़े हुए billers और payment channels एक common व्यवस्था से काम करते हैं। Electricity, mobile, gas और insurance जैसे bills इसके उदाहरण हैं।
beats.on_screen: Expand BBPS; bring electricity, mobile, gas and insurance bills onto one platform.

beats.say: Interoperable का मतलब दुनिया का हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं है; participation जरूरी है। और Bank Mitra से cash withdrawal bill payment नहीं है, इसलिए उसे BBPS का उदाहरण नहीं कहोगे।
beats.on_screen: Participating billers only; contrast bill payment with assisted withdrawal.

beats.say: BBPS याद आए तो common platform पर अलग-अलग bills भरना सोचो। AEPS की पहचान Aadhaar-biometric banking access है; shared NPCI link होने पर भी दोनों interchangeable नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: BBPS: bills; AEPS: identity-based banking access.

beats.say: अब जरूरत देखकर system पहचानो: transfer में amount, urgency और settlement; banking से दूर व्यक्ति के लिए assisted access; household के लिए common bill payment। Exam में availability को speed, minimum को maximum और operator को regulator मत बना देना।
beats.on_screen: Choose by need; check timing, thresholds, conditions and institutional roles.

replace_beats.say: Rent, supplier payment और बिजली का bill—क्या तीनों के लिए वही system चुनोगे? Amount, urgency और काम देखकर चुनना होगा।
Sunday रात घर पैसे भेजने हों तो? NEFT 24×7, free of cost और regular transfers के लिए suitable है, जैसे घर का खर्च भेजना।
Supplier को बड़ा payment चाहिए तो RTGS high-value transfers के लिए है। इसे सीधे RBI चलाता है; instruction तुम अपने bank को देते हो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer bank connects to RBI-operated RTGS.

replace_beats.say: रात में urgent payment हो तो IMPS immediate transfer देता है, round the clock। Bank के app या website से instruction दे सकते हो।
replace_beats.on_screen: IMPS: immediate; mobile and internet banking.

replace_beats.say: IMPS की range ₹1–₹5 lakh, यानी ₹500000 तक दी गई है। NEFT के लिए भी mainly ₹5 lakh तक, bank के अनुसार बदलने वाली limit है। RTGS sender fee ₹50 तक allowed है, compulsory ₹50 नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Range, bank limit and fee ceiling in separate boxes.

replace_beats.say: लेकिन comparison में NEFT maximum ‘No fixed limit’, IMPS minimum ‘No minimum’ है; wording का फर्क रखो। IMPS में instant, 24×7 फिर मिलते हैं; channels में ATM भी है।
RTGS का ₹2 lakh minimum उसके high-value use को समझाता है; institutional matching भी RBI है। NEFT regular transfers के लिए है; free को हर channel की verified fee policy मत समझना।
replace_beats.on_screen: RTGS threshold and RBI link; NEFT fee qualification.

replace_beats.say: याद रखो: primary use का मतलब only use नहीं; bank limit system ceiling नहीं; allowed fee compulsory fee नहीं।
अलग समय के payments साथ process हों तो? Jaipur के इस example में Meena का ₹2000 rent, Ravi का ₹3000 आटा payment, Saira की ₹1000 fee है।
10:00 round के बाद instructions 10:05, 10:12, 10:22 पर आए; waiting count 0 से 3 हुआ। मानो तीनों 10:30 round के लिए eligible हैं।
₹6000 का group process हुआ: यही NEFT batching, यानी transfers साथ process करना, हर आधे घंटे। Transfer पूरा होने पर Meena का balance ₹10000→₹8000, landlord का ₹1000→₹3000 होगा, charges छोड़कर।
replace_beats.on_screen: Batch processing followed by completed customer credit.

replace_beats.say: अब steel payment को इंतज़ार क्यों कराएँ? Jaipur के दूसरे example में Kavita, Bank A से Arjun के Bank B को ₹300000 भेजती है; valid instruction और enough funds मानो।
RBI settlement balances: Bank A ₹1000000→₹700000, Bank B ₹1000000→₹1300000। Customer balances अलग हैं: completion पर Kavita ₹500000→₹200000, Arjun ₹100000→₹400000, charges छोड़कर।

बाद का ₹200000 refund भी अलग पूरा settle हुआ: Arjun के ₹200000, Kavita के ₹400000 बचे। सिर्फ ₹100000 difference settle नहीं हुआ। यही RTGS: real-time gross settlement, हर payment पूरा अलग; no batching, 24×7।
replace_beats.on_screen: Two full-value arrows, not one net-difference arrow.

replace_beats.say: 10:30 batch time, exact credit deadline नहीं है। Invalid instruction या funds की कमी में RTGS की success भी मत मानो।
Rent और fees group में गए; steel payment और refund अलग पूरे settle हुए। Urgency में अगली processing round का इंतज़ार हटना उपयोगी है।
NEFT flow: instruction, batch, processing, credit। RTGS में हर valid payment का full-value settlement अलग, batch का इंतज़ार नहीं।
Phone पर चार choices में common क्या है? NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI चारों 24×7, all days हैं; timing अकेले चुनाव नहीं कराती।

NEFT है National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement; IMPS, Immediate Payment Service; UPI, Unified Payments Interface। Interface यानी payment इस्तेमाल करने का रास्ता, जैसे phone screen; खुद bank नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Full forms; highlight each name's cue.

replace_beats.say: Matching में NEFT–RTGS के साथ RBI, IMPS–UPI के साथ NPCI है। लेकिन network चलाने वाला operator और rules की देखरेख करने वाला regulator अलग हैं; overarching regulation RBI का है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Separate operator association from regulatory oversight.

replace_beats.say: NEFT batch-based होने से slower है, जैसे group तैयार होने तक रुकना। RTGS real-time gross, high-value में instant; IMPS–UPI real-time और instant बताए जाते हैं—यह user experience है, पूरे interbank settlement की explanation नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Batch queue versus immediate user transfer; settlement caveat.

replace_beats.say: RTGS minimum ₹2 lakh; बाकी तीनों में no minimum। इसलिए ₹50000 नीचे, ₹200000 threshold पर है। NEFT maximum no fixed limit, RTGS no upper limit; bank-channel conditions फिर भी देखो।

IMPS maximum ₹5 lakh, bank variation के साथ। UPI figures ₹1 lakh default, ₹10 lakh Person-to-Merchant हैं; enhanced limit eligible category और conditions पर है, हर merchant QR पर नहीं। NEFT का bank-qualified ₹5 lakh universal ceiling नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Conditional numerical maxima versus no system-wide numerical ceiling.

replace_beats.say: Use में NEFT regular, RTGS high-value urgent, IMPS everyday urgent है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer और merchant payment है, यानी दोस्त या दुकानदार को पैसे देना।
NEFT–RTGS: internet और mobile banking; IMPS: इनके साथ ATM; UPI: GPay, PhonePe जैसे apps। Channel service का दरवाज़ा है, system खुद नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Access doors lead to underlying systems.

replace_beats.say: NEFT में group का इंतज़ार speed घटाता है। RTGS threshold high-value use से जुड़ता है; gross का मतलब बड़ा amount नहीं, पूरा अलग settlement है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Separate timing, amount and gross settlement.

replace_beats.say: Statement trap: ‘दोनों 24×7, इसलिए दोनों instant।’ नहीं—खुला counter भी group का इंतज़ार करा सकता है। RTGS का ₹2 lakh entry gate है, ceiling नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Cross out availability implies instant; label minimum gate.

replace_beats.say: पहले amount और urgency, फिर limit और channel देखो। NEFT regular, RTGS बड़ा urgent, IMPS everyday urgent, UPI दोस्त-दुकान payments से जोड़ो।
Counter पर Aadhaar से service मिले तो? AEPS है Aadhaar Enabled Payment System; enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद। नाम अकेले पूरा procedure नहीं बताता।
replace_beats.on_screen: AEPS expansion; name distinct from procedure.

replace_beats.say: दो अलग services का common link क्या है? AEPS और BBPS दोनों का management NPCI से जुड़ा है; काम समान नहीं हो जाता।
replace_beats.on_screen: NPCI linked to two distinct services.

replace_beats.say: AEPS में Aadhaar पहचान का cue है; दोनों services का institutional link NPCI है। अब काम अलग देखो।
Branch दूर, ₹500 cash चाहिए तो? Village counter पर authorised withdrawal के बाद customer को ₹500 मिले; balance ₹1000→₹500 हुआ।
वहाँ Aadhaar और biometrics, यानी उँगली के निशान जैसी पहचान, इस्तेमाल हुई। Bank Mitra bank की service पहुँचाने वाला मददगार है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer, Bank Mitra and fingerprint scanner.

replace_beats.say: पहले identity check, फिर authorised withdrawal और debit: यह AEPS access है। Authentication और payment Bank Mitras से होते हैं; पहचान जाँचना पैसे देना नहीं।
Authentication fail हो तो transaction authorised मत मानो; पास का counter success की guarantee नहीं।
Identity check, authorisation, banking service—पास में मदद से दूर branch जाने की मुश्किल घटती है। यही financial inclusion, banking से दूर लोगों को जोड़ना है।
AEPS में Aadhaar-biometric पहचान और Bank Mitra की मदद से banking access मिलता है; मुख्य उद्देश्य financial inclusion है।
Subsidy आए, पर access न हो तो? मानो ₹500 government credit से balance ₹0→₹500 हुआ; उसे इस्तेमाल भी करना है।
Beneficiary Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric access लेता है। Credit होना और पैसे इस्तेमाल कर पाना अलग जरूरतें हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Account credit distinct from later access.

replace_beats.say: यह AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को support करना है: सरकारी मदद सीधे beneficiary तक, फिर local access से उसका इस्तेमाल।
Grassroots तक subsidies पहुँचने का मतलब गाँव के beneficiary को भी banking access मिलना है, केवल account होना नहीं।
AEPS subsidy eligibility तय नहीं करता; यह credited benefit तक banking access देता है।
Chain है: government credit, पास में banking access, फिर usable benefit; inclusion से मदद इस्तेमाल करना आसान होता है।
अलग bills एक रास्ते से भरें तो? Household participating electricity biller चुनता है; ₹600 payment settle होने पर due ₹600→₹0 होता है।
यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: single interoperable platform, यानी जुड़े billers और channels साथ काम करें। Electricity, mobile, gas, insurance bills इसके उदाहरण हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Several bill types join one common platform.

replace_beats.say: हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं; participation चाहिए। Bank Mitra से cash withdrawal भी BBPS bill payment नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Participating billers only; withdrawal is non-example.

replace_beats.say: BBPS common bill payment है, AEPS Aadhaar-biometric banking access। NPCI link साझा है, services interchangeable नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: BBPS bills versus AEPS assisted banking.

replace_beats.say: अब जरूरत से system चुनो: transfer, assisted banking या bills। Availability को speed, minimum को maximum और operator को regulator मत समझना।

beats.say: RBI settlement balances: Bank A ₹1000000→₹700000, Bank B ₹1000000→₹1300000। Customer balances अलग हैं: completion पर Kavita ₹500000→₹200000, Arjun ₹100000→₹400000, charges छोड़कर।
beats.on_screen: Separate interbank and customer ledgers.

beats.say: बाद का ₹200000 refund भी अलग पूरा settle हुआ: Arjun के ₹200000, Kavita के ₹400000 बचे। सिर्फ ₹100000 difference settle नहीं हुआ। यही RTGS: real-time gross settlement, हर payment पूरा अलग; no batching, 24×7।
beats.on_screen: Two full-value arrows, not one net-difference arrow.

beats.say: 10:30 batch time, exact credit deadline नहीं है। Invalid instruction या funds की कमी में RTGS की success भी मत मानो।
beats.on_screen: Processing time ≠ guaranteed credit time.

beats.say: Rent और fees group में गए; steel payment और refund अलग पूरे settle हुए। Urgency में अगली processing round का इंतज़ार हटना उपयोगी है।
beats.on_screen: Replay both mechanisms.

beats.say: NEFT flow: instruction, batch, processing, credit। RTGS में हर valid payment का full-value settlement अलग, batch का इंतज़ार नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two flow summaries.

beats.say: Phone पर चार choices में common क्या है? NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI चारों 24×7, all days हैं; timing अकेले चुनाव नहीं कराती।
beats.on_screen: Shared availability clock.

beats.say: NEFT है National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement; IMPS, Immediate Payment Service; UPI, Unified Payments Interface। Interface यानी payment इस्तेमाल करने का रास्ता, जैसे phone screen; खुद bank नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Full forms; highlight each name's cue.

beats.say: Matching में NEFT–RTGS के साथ RBI, IMPS–UPI के साथ NPCI है। लेकिन network चलाने वाला operator और rules की देखरेख करने वाला regulator अलग हैं; overarching regulation RBI का है।
beats.on_screen: Separate operator association from regulatory oversight.

beats.say: NEFT batch-based होने से slower है, जैसे group तैयार होने तक रुकना। RTGS real-time gross, high-value में instant; IMPS–UPI real-time और instant बताए जाते हैं—यह user experience है, पूरे interbank settlement की explanation नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Batch queue versus immediate user transfer; settlement caveat.

beats.say: RTGS minimum ₹2 lakh; बाकी तीनों में no minimum। इसलिए ₹50000 नीचे, ₹200000 threshold पर है। NEFT maximum no fixed limit, RTGS no upper limit; bank-channel conditions फिर भी देखो।
beats.on_screen: Minimum gate versus upper ceiling.

beats.say: IMPS maximum ₹5 lakh, bank variation के साथ। UPI figures ₹1 lakh default, ₹10 lakh Person-to-Merchant हैं; enhanced limit eligible category और conditions पर है, हर merchant QR पर नहीं। NEFT का bank-qualified ₹5 lakh universal ceiling नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Conditional numerical maxima versus no system-wide numerical ceiling.

beats.say: Use में NEFT regular, RTGS high-value urgent, IMPS everyday urgent है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer और merchant payment है, यानी दोस्त या दुकानदार को पैसे देना।
beats.on_screen: Four typical payment situations.

beats.say: NEFT–RTGS: internet और mobile banking; IMPS: इनके साथ ATM; UPI: GPay, PhonePe जैसे apps। Channel service का दरवाज़ा है, system खुद नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Access doors lead to underlying systems.

beats.say: NEFT में group का इंतज़ार speed घटाता है। RTGS threshold high-value use से जुड़ता है; gross का मतलब बड़ा amount नहीं, पूरा अलग settlement है।
beats.on_screen: Separate timing, amount and gross settlement.

beats.say: Statement trap: ‘दोनों 24×7, इसलिए दोनों instant।’ नहीं—खुला counter भी group का इंतज़ार करा सकता है। RTGS का ₹2 lakh entry gate है, ceiling नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Cross out availability implies instant; label minimum gate.

beats.say: पहले amount और urgency, फिर limit और channel देखो। NEFT regular, RTGS बड़ा urgent, IMPS everyday urgent, UPI दोस्त-दुकान payments से जोड़ो।
beats.on_screen: Compact comparison table.

beats.say: Counter पर Aadhaar से service मिले तो? AEPS है Aadhaar Enabled Payment System; enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद। नाम अकेले पूरा procedure नहीं बताता।
beats.on_screen: AEPS expansion; name distinct from procedure.

beats.say: दो अलग services का common link क्या है? AEPS और BBPS दोनों का management NPCI से जुड़ा है; काम समान नहीं हो जाता।
beats.on_screen: NPCI linked to two distinct services.

beats.say: AEPS में Aadhaar पहचान का cue है; दोनों services का institutional link NPCI है। अब काम अलग देखो।
beats.on_screen: Name cue versus institutional association.

beats.say: Branch दूर, ₹500 cash चाहिए तो? Village counter पर authorised withdrawal के बाद customer को ₹500 मिले; balance ₹1000→₹500 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative withdrawal outcome.

beats.say: वहाँ Aadhaar और biometrics, यानी उँगली के निशान जैसी पहचान, इस्तेमाल हुई। Bank Mitra bank की service पहुँचाने वाला मददगार है।
beats.on_screen: Customer, Bank Mitra and fingerprint scanner.

beats.say: पहले identity check, फिर authorised withdrawal और debit: यह AEPS access है। Authentication और payment Bank Mitras से होते हैं; पहचान जाँचना पैसे देना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Authentication precedes transaction.

beats.say: Authentication fail हो तो transaction authorised मत मानो; पास का counter success की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops authorised flow.

beats.say: Identity check, authorisation, banking service—पास में मदद से दूर branch जाने की मुश्किल घटती है। यही financial inclusion, banking से दूर लोगों को जोड़ना है।
beats.on_screen: Local access reduces branch-access barrier.

beats.say: AEPS में Aadhaar-biometric पहचान और Bank Mitra की मदद से banking access मिलता है; मुख्य उद्देश्य financial inclusion है।
beats.on_screen: Identity → assisted banking → inclusion.

beats.say: Subsidy आए, पर access न हो तो? मानो ₹500 government credit से balance ₹0→₹500 हुआ; उसे इस्तेमाल भी करना है।
beats.on_screen: Credit complete; access barrier remains.

beats.say: Beneficiary Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric access लेता है। Credit होना और पैसे इस्तेमाल कर पाना अलग जरूरतें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Account credit distinct from later access.

beats.say: यह AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को support करना है: सरकारी मदद सीधे beneficiary तक, फिर local access से उसका इस्तेमाल।
beats.on_screen: Government → account → local access.

beats.say: Grassroots तक subsidies पहुँचने का मतलब गाँव के beneficiary को भी banking access मिलना है, केवल account होना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Zoom to village beneficiary.

beats.say: AEPS subsidy eligibility तय नहीं करता; यह credited benefit तक banking access देता है।
beats.on_screen: Eligibility ≠ access.

beats.say: Chain है: government credit, पास में banking access, फिर usable benefit; inclusion से मदद इस्तेमाल करना आसान होता है।
beats.on_screen: Credit → access → usable benefit.

beats.say: अलग bills एक रास्ते से भरें तो? Household participating electricity biller चुनता है; ₹600 payment settle होने पर due ₹600→₹0 होता है।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative electricity bill payment.

beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: single interoperable platform, यानी जुड़े billers और channels साथ काम करें। Electricity, mobile, gas, insurance bills इसके उदाहरण हैं।
beats.on_screen: Several bill types join one common platform.

beats.say: हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं; participation चाहिए। Bank Mitra से cash withdrawal भी BBPS bill payment नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Participating billers only; withdrawal is non-example.

beats.say: BBPS common bill payment है, AEPS Aadhaar-biometric banking access। NPCI link साझा है, services interchangeable नहीं।
beats.on_screen: BBPS bills versus AEPS assisted banking.

beats.say: अब जरूरत से system चुनो: transfer, assisted banking या bills। Availability को speed, minimum को maximum और operator को regulator मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Choose by need; check conditions.

beats.say: Sunday रात घर पैसे भेजने हों तो? NEFT 24×7, free of cost और regular transfers के लिए suitable है, जैसे घर का खर्च भेजना।

beats.say: बाद का ₹200000 refund भी अलग पूरा settle हुआ: Arjun के ₹200000, Kavita के ₹400000 बचे। सिर्फ ₹100000 difference settle नहीं हुआ। यही RTGS, यानी real-time gross settlement है: हर payment पूरा अलग settle होता है, batching नहीं होती; service 24×7 उपलब्ध है।
beats.on_screen: Two full-value arrows, not one net-difference arrow.

beats.say: 10:30 batch time, exact credit deadline नहीं है। Invalid instruction या funds की कमी में RTGS की success भी मत मानो।
beats.on_screen: Processing time ≠ guaranteed credit time.

beats.say: Rent और fees group में गए; steel payment और refund अलग पूरे settle हुए। Urgency में अगली processing round का इंतज़ार हटना उपयोगी है।
beats.on_screen: Replay both mechanisms.

beats.say: NEFT flow: instruction, batch, processing, credit। RTGS में हर valid payment का full-value settlement अलग, batch का इंतज़ार नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two flow summaries.

beats.say: Phone पर चार choices में common क्या है? NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI चारों 24×7, all days हैं; timing अकेले चुनाव नहीं कराती।
beats.on_screen: Shared availability clock.

beats.say: NEFT है National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement; IMPS, Immediate Payment Service; UPI, Unified Payments Interface। Interface यानी payment इस्तेमाल करने का रास्ता, जैसे phone screen; खुद bank नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Full forms; highlight each name's cue.

beats.say: Matching में NEFT–RTGS के साथ RBI, IMPS–UPI के साथ NPCI है। लेकिन network चलाने वाला operator और regulator अलग हैं; payments का overarching regulatory oversight RBI करता है।
beats.on_screen: Separate operator association from regulatory oversight.

beats.say: NEFT batch-based होने से slower है, जैसे group तैयार होने तक रुकना। RTGS real-time gross, high-value में instant; IMPS–UPI real-time और instant बताए जाते हैं—यह user experience है, पूरे interbank settlement की explanation नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Batch queue versus immediate user transfer; settlement caveat.

beats.say: RTGS minimum ₹2 lakh; बाकी तीनों में no minimum। इसलिए ₹50000 नीचे, ₹200000 threshold पर है। NEFT maximum no fixed limit, RTGS no upper limit; bank-channel conditions फिर भी देखो।
beats.on_screen: Minimum gate versus upper ceiling.

beats.say: IMPS maximum ₹5 lakh है, जो bank के अनुसार बदलता है। UPI figures ₹1 lakh default, ₹10 lakh Person-to-Merchant हैं; enhanced limit eligible category और conditions पर है, हर merchant QR पर नहीं। NEFT का bank-qualified ₹5 lakh universal ceiling नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Conditional numerical maxima versus no system-wide numerical ceiling.

beats.say: Use में NEFT regular, RTGS high-value urgent, IMPS everyday urgent है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer और merchant payment है, यानी दोस्त या दुकानदार को पैसे देना।
beats.on_screen: Four typical payment situations.

beats.say: NEFT–RTGS internet और mobile banking से इस्तेमाल होते हैं। IMPS में ATM भी शामिल है; UPI में GPay, PhonePe जैसे apps हैं। Channel service का दरवाज़ा है, system खुद नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Access doors lead to underlying systems.

beats.say: NEFT में group का इंतज़ार speed घटाता है। RTGS threshold high-value use से जुड़ता है; gross का मतलब बड़ा amount नहीं, पूरा अलग settlement है।
beats.on_screen: Separate timing, amount and gross settlement.

beats.say: Statement trap: ‘दोनों 24×7, इसलिए दोनों instant।’ नहीं—खुला counter भी group का इंतज़ार करा सकता है। RTGS का ₹2 lakh entry gate है, ceiling नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Cross out availability implies instant; label minimum gate.

beats.say: पहले amount और urgency, फिर limit और channel देखो। NEFT regular, RTGS बड़ा urgent, IMPS everyday urgent, UPI दोस्त-दुकान payments से जोड़ो।
beats.on_screen: Compact comparison table.

beats.say: Counter पर Aadhaar से service मिले तो? AEPS है Aadhaar Enabled Payment System; enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद। नाम अकेले पूरा procedure नहीं बताता।
beats.on_screen: AEPS expansion; name distinct from procedure.

beats.say: दो अलग services का common link क्या है? AEPS और BBPS दोनों का management NPCI से जुड़ा है; काम समान नहीं हो जाता।
beats.on_screen: NPCI linked to two distinct services.

beats.say: AEPS में Aadhaar पहचान का cue है; दोनों services का institutional link NPCI है। अब काम अलग देखो।
beats.on_screen: Name cue versus institutional association.

beats.say: Branch दूर, ₹500 cash चाहिए तो? Village counter पर authorised withdrawal के बाद customer को ₹500 मिले; balance ₹1000→₹500 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative withdrawal outcome.

beats.say: वहाँ Aadhaar और biometrics, यानी उँगली के निशान जैसी पहचान, इस्तेमाल हुई। Bank Mitra bank की service पहुँचाने वाला मददगार है।
beats.on_screen: Customer, Bank Mitra and fingerprint scanner.

beats.say: पहले identity check, फिर authorised withdrawal और debit: यह AEPS access है। Authentication और payment Bank Mitras से होते हैं; पहचान जाँचना पैसे देना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Authentication precedes transaction.

beats.say: Authentication fail हो तो transaction authorised मत मानो; पास का counter success की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops authorised flow.

beats.say: Identity check, authorisation, banking service—पास में मदद से दूर branch जाने की मुश्किल घटती है। यही financial inclusion, banking से दूर लोगों को जोड़ना है।
beats.on_screen: Local access reduces branch-access barrier.

beats.say: AEPS में Aadhaar-biometric पहचान और Bank Mitra की मदद से banking access मिलता है; मुख्य उद्देश्य financial inclusion है।
beats.on_screen: Identity → assisted banking → inclusion.

beats.say: Subsidy आए, पर access न हो तो? मानो ₹500 government credit से balance ₹0→₹500 हुआ; उसे इस्तेमाल भी करना है।
beats.on_screen: Credit complete; access barrier remains.

beats.say: Beneficiary Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric access लेता है। Credit होना और पैसे इस्तेमाल कर पाना अलग जरूरतें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Account credit distinct from later access.

beats.say: यह AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को support करना है: सरकारी मदद सीधे beneficiary तक, फिर local access से उसका इस्तेमाल।
beats.on_screen: Government → account → local access.

beats.say: Grassroots तक subsidies पहुँचने का मतलब गाँव के beneficiary को भी banking access मिलना है, केवल account होना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Zoom to village beneficiary.

beats.say: AEPS subsidy eligibility तय नहीं करता; यह credited benefit तक banking access देता है।
beats.on_screen: Eligibility ≠ access.

beats.say: Chain है: government credit, पास में banking access, फिर usable benefit; inclusion से मदद इस्तेमाल करना आसान होता है।
beats.on_screen: Credit → access → usable benefit.

beats.say: अलग bills एक रास्ते से भरें तो? Household participating electricity biller चुनता है; ₹600 payment settle होने पर due ₹600→₹0 होता है।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative electricity bill payment.

beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: single interoperable platform, यानी जुड़े billers और channels साथ काम करें। Electricity, mobile, gas, insurance bills इसके उदाहरण हैं।
beats.on_screen: Several bill types join one common platform.

beats.say: हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं; participation चाहिए। Bank Mitra से cash withdrawal भी BBPS bill payment नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Participating billers only; withdrawal is non-example.

beats.say: BBPS common bill payment है, AEPS Aadhaar-biometric banking access। NPCI link साझा है, services interchangeable नहीं।
beats.on_screen: BBPS bills versus AEPS assisted banking.

beats.say: जरूरत से system चुनो; availability, speed, limits और institutional roles अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Choose by need; distinguish availability, speed, limits and institutional roles.

notes.about: This unit compares four transfer systems and distinguishes Aadhaar-assisted banking access from interoperable bill payment. Coverage is broad and most substantive qualifications are preserved, but example-first teaching and some explanatory steps remain incomplete.
key_questions: How do availability, speed and settlement differ?
Which amount and fee statements are conditional rather than universal?
How does AEPS make credited benefits accessible, and how does BBPS connect billers and channels?

problems.problem: NEFT, RTGS and AEPS are named and assigned their mechanisms before their required numerical examples run. Even within the NEFT example, b11 names batching before completing the balance changes. This reverses the explicit example → term → definition sequence.
problems.fix: Open with the numerical NEFT and RTGS stories, complete each money movement, then introduce its term and service facts. Move AEPS naming until after the withdrawal and authentication example. Fund this reordering by removing repeated previews and recaps in b7–b8, b16–b17 and b31.

problems.problem: Several comparison facts remain compressed lists rather than opened teaching. In particular, 'default' is never explained, Person-to-Merchant is not plainly defined, and the full-form beat does not explain what the names emphasise despite claiming p014-i8#q2. The amount comparisons mostly announce thresholds rather than showing the consequences across services.
problems.fix: Explain default as the ordinarily applicable starting limit and Person-to-Merchant as a person paying a business. Explicitly connect electronic transfer, gross settlement, immediate payment and interface to the four names. Run one amount-choice example across the relevant services, retaining all qualifications. Replace repeated use summaries in b24, b26 and b28 rather than adding duration.

problems.problem: Phrases such as 'comparison में', 'फिर मिलते हैं', 'बताए जाते हैं' and 'UPI figures ... हैं' report source wording instead of consistently teaching the facts directly. Conversely, conditional or source-specific fee and UPI figures are not clearly distinguished from independently verified current rules in the spoken narration.
problems.fix: Teach the operational distinctions directly without referring to a comparison or repeated wording. Put explicit source-status qualifications in non-spoken provenance labels for the printed fee and limit claims; retain spoken warnings against universal application. Replace the existing reporting phrases rather than lengthening these beats.

problems.problem: Closely spaced recaps repeat conclusions already stated, consuming space needed for explanations.
problems.fix: Combine the fast process replay with its visual flow recap and remove umbrella recaps that add no new distinction.
